mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate level is causally linked to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reduces the cost of capital for corporations and increases the present value of future cash flows.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a rolling 5-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A tight labor market, indicated by unemployment rate below 4.0%, signals potential inflationary pressures and impending monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 4.0%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC for UNRATE as a predictor falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate and consumer price inflation signal a monetary tightening cycle in response to persistent inflation, which compresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL in a regression of 20-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) or the Rank IC for the interaction signal falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of strong economic growth (GDPC1 annualized growth rate > 2%), new housing starts (HOUST) are a leading indicator of consumer spending and corporate investment, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In high GDP growth regimes (GDPC1 annualized growth > 2%), the correlation between HOUST and 20-day S&P 500 returns is not positive (Rank IC <= 0.03) or the effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (the 2017 base) signals a weakening manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 100, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% annualized signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, which reduces equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for CPIAUCSL 12m %ch as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns is below 0.03 in any 3-year window, or CPIAUCSL 12m %ch > 3.0% does not lead to negative returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Higher new housing starts (HOUST) are a leading indicator of consumer spending and economic activity, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for HOUST as a predictor of 60-day S&P 500 returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between HOUST and 60-day returns is not positive (Rank IC <= 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) combined with rising retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term between PAYEMS and RSAFS in a regression of 20-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) or the Rank IC for the interaction signal falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
